Common questions

Why am I getting false alerts?

The most common cause is a check interval that's too short relative to your endpoint's cold-start or GC pause behavior. Try:

  • Increasing after_failures to 2 or 3 — this requires n consecutive failures before firing
  • Increasing timeout_s to accommodate occasional slow responses
  • Using multi-region probes — if only one region fails, it's likely a network issue, not a service outage

My webhook isn't receiving events

Check the webhook delivery log: GET /v1/webhooks/{id}/deliveries. Common causes:

  • Your endpoint returned a non-2xx response — SignalForge marks the delivery as failed and will retry
  • Your endpoint took longer than 10 seconds to respond — webhook delivery times out at 10s
  • Your firewall is blocking outbound requests from SignalForge's IP ranges — see IP ranges
  • The webhook destination is not configured in the correct alert rule or monitor's alert block

How do I upgrade my config from v0.8.x?

Run the migration command. It reads your current signalforge.yml, applies the v0.9.x schema changes, and writes a new file. Review the diff before committing.

bash 
$ signalforge migrate --from 0.8 --dry-run

Migration: 0.8.x → 0.9.x

  ~ Renamed top-level `notify` → per-monitor `alert` blocks
  ~ Moved global destinations to top-level `destinations` array

No breaking changes detected. Apply with --write flag.
$ signalforge migrate --from 0.8 --write

I'm hitting rate limits on the API

The free tier allows 60 reads/min and 20 writes/min. If you're hitting this while building a dashboard or integration, consider:

  • Polling GET /v1/signals with a since timestamp rather than fetching all signals each time
  • Using webhooks for real-time signal delivery instead of polling
  • Upgrading to the Pro tier (300 reads/min, 100 writes/min)
